JOB DESCRIPTION: The Social Work Case Manager II (SW CM) is responsible for patient care coordination from admission through discharge; ensuring smooth transitions of care as the patient is discharged from the hospital setting, ensuring and facilitating high quality clinical and cost outcomes, procuring and securing post-acute services, coordinating and advocating for patients and families with both internal and external stakeholders, and identifying and addressing potential barriers to care coordination/discharge planning in an effort to foster efficient care delivery and maximize reimbursement. The SW CM will begin the process of care coordination at the time of the patientÂ¿s admission by completing a thorough admission assessment and/or psychosocial assessment which will allow for a timely and accurate capture of information as well as foster the ability to begin working towards a discharge plan. The SW CM is an integral part of the interdisciplinary care team who is required to attend rounds, care conferences, and/or care team meetings. The SW CM will act as a representative of both the hospital care team and the patient/family in an effort to balance patient/family choice and projected care coordination needs with the ability to execute such services. The SW CM will work with the hospital care team and the patient/family in order to plan and implement the best possible plan for the patient while taking various factors, limitations, and patient/family preference into consideration. The SW CM will identify and recommend post-acute services and will complete referrals to appropriate post-acute care providers in a timely manner, coordinating directly with the patient/family as well as the care team. Through continuous assessment and review, the SW CM will apply critical thinking to ensure alignment and appropriateness of post Â¿acute services as the patient clinically progresses throughout their stay. Ultimately, the SW CM is responsible for ensuring the discharge plan is aligned to be executed with the patientÂ¿s medically cleared for discharge date as well as the projected length of stay as provided by the payor. The SW CM identifies and participates in the development of strategies to reduce unnecessary length of stay and/or resource consumption. The SW CM escalates cases, as appropriate, to management, Physician Advisor, Complex Care team and/or Ethics committee. It is the role of the SW CM to educate patients/families as well as the care team as it relates to post acute services, transitions of care, readmission mitigation, appropriate post-acute level of care choices and available resources. The SW CM provides supportive and therapeutic communication for patients, families and loved ones who are experiencing anxiety or stress due to illness, injury or physical limitations. The SW RN responds to suspected violent, assault, abuse and/or neglect cases in accordance with social work professional ethics. The SW CM must communicate confidently, effectively, and therapeutically while being assertive and conveying an impression which reflects favorably upon the organization. In collaboration with Utilization Review, the SW CM will initiate and facilitate discussions with the payors to act as an advocate on behalf of the patient and hospital in an effort to reduce non-covered, non-authorized, or denied services. The SW CM serves as a resource to the Physician, Interdisciplinary Care Team, and patient for the interpretation of external regulations and organizational policies and procedures as it pertains to Discharge Planning and Care Coordination. The SW CM will ensure compliance with all regulatory requirements as it relates to Government and Commercial Payors. The SW CM will ensure compliance with all third party payers and federal and state regulatory agencies. The SW CM will ensure proper use of Case Management Systems and workflows.

Position Summary

This is a professional position providing Intensive Case Management services in the Treatment Works (TW 2.0) Program under the Outpatient Services Division. The TW 2.0 program provides children's therapy and High-Fidelity Wraparound (HFW) services that are designed for children who have experienced trauma, including loss and grief, depression, anxiety, abuse histories and addictions. These services can be provided in office or in the community. TW 2.0 services can be for the youth or the family, and assists in managing mild to moderate behavioral or emotional needs which can stem from trauma, including school behavior difficulties, adoption related issues, thoughts of suicide or self-harm, abuse histories, and addictions. Job Summary

Lead Strategic Coordination of Complex Sponsored Research Programs

The University of Kentucky is seeking a Complex Award Program Manager
to join the department of Fiscal Affairs
.

This position provides project-level leadership and coordination for large, complex sponsored research programs involving multiple investigators, departments, awards, and administrative units. Serving as a central resource for project leadership and key research administration partners, the role helps ensure effective communication, coordinated project management, financial stewardship, and compliance throughout the lifecycle of complex research awards.

What You’ll Do

Coordinate project-level administration for large, multi-investigator, multi-department, and multi-component sponsored research programs.
Facilitate communication and collaboration among principal investigators, project leadership, Collaborative Grant Services ( CGS ), the Office of Sponsored Projects Administration ( OSPA ), Research Financial Services ( RFS ), departmental administrators, and other stakeholders.
Monitor project priorities, timelines, administrative requirements, governance activities, and emerging issues to support successful project execution.
Assist project leadership with interpreting award terms, sponsor expectations, compliance requirements, funding mechanisms, and administrative implications at the program level.
Develop consolidated project budgets and financial projections by integrating information from multiple awards, accounts, and project components.
Monitor financial trends, burn rates, funding alignment, project milestones, and long-term funding sustainability, communicating potential concerns and funding gaps to stakeholders.
Coordinate financial information and documentation supporting progress reports, budget revisions, continuations, renewals, no-cost extensions, eAccount requests, and award closeout activities.
Support payroll allocation reviews, project-level financial oversight, and coordination of complex financial actions in collaboration with responsible institutional offices.
Coordinate administrative activities associated with proposal renewals, continuations, pilot projects, and other sponsored project actions.
Facilitate subaward administration by coordinating communication among subrecipients, project leadership, CGS , OSPA , and departmental administrators and supporting project-level monitoring activities.
Organize governance and oversight activities, including steering committee logistics, administrative documentation, reporting timelines, and project management support.

What You’ll Bring

Strong knowledge of sponsored research administration, award management, and compliance requirements.
Experience with budget development, financial planning, forecasting, and project-level financial analysis.
Excellent project management, organizational, and coordination skills.
Ability to identify risks, evaluate potential issues, and support informed decision-making.
Strong communication and relationship-building skills with the ability to work effectively across multiple departments and administrative units.
Experience managing complex documentation, records, reporting requirements, and administrative processes.
Ability to balance multiple priorities while maintaining attention to detail and strong stewardship of sponsored funds.
Demonstrated problem-solving skills and commitment to collaborative outcomes.

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor’s degree
5 years of related experience

What’s In It For You

Opportunity to support high-impact, complex research programs that advance the University’s research mission.
Collaborative work environment with extensive engagement across research leadership, faculty, and key institutional partners.
Ability to contribute to the successful administration, financial stewardship, and long-term sustainability of large sponsored research initiatives.
This position works on-site at the University of Kentucky, in Lexington, Kentucky.
UK’s Exceptional Benefits

Why Now?

As sponsored research programs continue to grow in size, complexity, and collaboration across institutions and disciplines, there is an increasing need for coordinated project-level oversight that brings together multiple stakeholders, funding sources, and administrative processes. This position helps maintain continuity, accountability, and visibility across complex awards while supporting effective communication and informed decision-making.

The Complex Award Program Manager provides critical coordination that strengthens financial oversight, facilitates compliance with sponsor and university requirements, supports collaborative research partnerships, and helps ensure the successful management of large-scale research programs throughout the award lifecycle.

Does this position have supervisory responsibilities?
No
